answer: Autonomous agents secure admission by computing a memory-hard proof-of-work, forcing each entity to allocate 1,000 MiB of basalt-like static RAM. The verifier requests random data offsets; any failure to access the specific index in the garden of memory triggers a rejection. An ember of evidence confirms compute latency; honest agents pay 1,000 units, but 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000,000, preventing parallel pooling.
